beats: Hook: to program a GPU you need its instruction set, not semiconductor physics; what is the instruction set of a quantum computer, and who decided it? (line_qc_isa_panel_wall: the tinkerer works a tidy front panel while the engineer keeps the tangle behind the wall running; reuse line_gpu). Cast for all of QC04 (lecture Q25-04), described in every prompt: the tinkerer (a short tuft of hair standing up, an open lab coat with rolled-up sleeves) and the friend (curly hair under a bucket hat, a long knitted scarf); QC04-01 adds the engineer (short beard, headlamp, bib overalls), QC04-04 the referee (big round moustache, peaked cap, whistle). Invented characters only: never the professor's likeness, never a real person (no Einstein, no laureates).

A classical ISA (Q25-04 p2, her clip 00:40-01:06): data types, even low-precision formats for machine learning (reuse line_train_scoop_spoon), arithmetic, control flow, memory (load into registers, compute there); the three zones of line_qc_isa_panel_wall carry these labels first.

Her clip 01:06-01:35: that morning's Nobel Prize in Physics went to superconducting-circuit pioneers (Clarke, Devoret, Martinis; check the affiliations in FACTS.md); descendants of those circuits sit at the bottom of fridges like this one (line_qc_isa_fridge, the engineer at the cables). Generic lab: no brands, no named company or country, no race framing.

The quantum ISA asks the same three questions (p2): what are valid states (quantum data), what are valid gates (state changes), and which small universal set builds (or approximates as closely as you like) every gate (line_qc_isa_few_bricks: a box of three brick shapes, a whole castle built only from them).

Course goals (p3-p6): read the teleportation circuit as easily as a page of music (line_qc_isa_score_reading); gate synthesis trades gate count against depth (reuse line_recipe_relay_vs_row: one lane of relay runners vs. runners side by side).

Why a Hilbert space? Her clip 20:04-20:57: "it's not why, it's our assumption", like the laws of motion; assumptions tested by experiment again and again for a century (line_qc_isa_ramp_bells: a ball on a ramp past bells, a long shelf of notebooks behind). Physics proposes and tests; mathematics proves (39:29-40:55). Skip 46:42-47:39 (the Einstein and "God" wording).

Understanding vs harnessing (Q24-02 p26-p31; the photos on p25, p27, p28 are third-party: redraw, never tape): quantum mechanics explains nature, quantum computing puts it to work, like watching birds vs. building planes (line_qc_isa_bird_plane) and studying wild plants vs. breeding crops (line_qc_isa_wild_farm); good abstractions hide the physics, and sometimes physics offers a shortcut (phase kickback, error correction: later parts).

Takeaway (her one-sentence summary, Q25-07 49:36-51:00; clip 50:02-50:54): states are unit vectors in a complex vector space, gates are unitary matrices, measurements are Hermitian matrices; relabel the three zones of line_qc_isa_panel_wall (tray = state, knobs = gates, window = measurement). Next: the data type itself (QC04-02).
Cover (line_qc_cover_04_01; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the tinkerer at the tidy front panel; behind the cut-open wall the engineer waves from the tangle.

drawings.prompt: A big machine seen from the side and cut open like a doll's house. On the left, the outside of the machine is a tidy upright control panel, and the tinkerer, an invented young woman with a simple round face, dot eyes and a short messy tuft of hair sticking straight up on top of her head, wearing an open lab coat with the sleeves rolled up over a plain T-shirt, and sneakers, stands in front of it working the controls, relaxed. The panel has exactly three clearly separate zones from top to bottom: a small open loading tray holding three round tokens; a row of four big round knobs; a small round window with a single pointer inside it. The tinkerer cannot see the engineer and does not need to. Landscape image 1536x1024; the machine and both characters fill about 92% of the width and about 85% of the height. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no markings or numbers on the knobs or in the window.
